content.text:
Here's the recap for the One More Morning flight (Jan 5–17, 2027, Africa/Johannesburg):

**Campaign:** "One More Morning — Jan 2027" (id 10lig), 4 ad groups on X, LINK_CLICKS goal, ALL_ON_TWITTER placements, worldwide targeting with China excluded (per the landing page's terms). Post 2138938279327834804 ("Something new from me…") was not promoted — it was the weakest fit among the approved copy. The other four posts ran; Post C (2138757085397349696) was paused on Jan 6 after the weakest CTR (~0.024%) and its budget shifted to the stronger posts; Post B (fresh-start copy) got the biggest allocation mid-flight.

**Totals (summed from the stats windows pulled):**
- Spend: ~$93.50 of the $100 budget
- Impressions: ~715K
- Link clicks: ~482 (Post A ~153, Post B ~190, Post C ~5, Post E ~134)

**Important distinction:** those ~482 are X link clicks — people who tapped the ad through to sivrocurrent.com. They are not your counted streams. Sivro Stream plays can't be tracked from X (no pixel on the site, and no web event tag exists in the account), so I have no visibility into actual streams; streams are only measurable inside Sivro Stream itself. The click numbers are an upper bound on landing-page visits, and an even looser proxy for streams.

**What worked:** Post B ("Keep that fresh-start feeling moving…") delivered the most clicks per dollar; Post C underperformed and was cut early. Posts A and E were mid-pack.

Caveats: figures are billed/reported values summed across two query windows and may not reconcile to the cent; the campaign auto-ended at 2027-01-17 22:00 UTC (midnight Johannesburg, end of Jan 17).
